merger_description:
Alter Domus Nederland B.V. (**Alter Domus**), an indirect wholly-owned subsidiary of Alter Domus Global S.à r.l. (or another wholly-owned subsidiary), proposes to acquire 100% of the issued share capital in MSC Group Co Pty Ltd (**MSC**) from its existing shareholders pursuant to a Share Sale Agreement (the **Acquisition**).

Alter Domus Group is a global provider of fund administration, private debt administration, and corporate services, dedicated exclusively to the alternative investment industry, with more than 6,500 staff across 39 offices worldwide. In Australia, Alter Domus is focused on fund administration for wholesale fund managers targeting wholesale investors in the alternative investments space.

MSC Group is an Australian-headquartered provider of professional trustee, custody, financial intermediary and fund administration services. Its core business is in the provision of custody and trustee services, with ancillary service offerings including fund administration.

Alter Domus is indirectly controlled by the Eighth Cinven Fund which is managed and controlled by Cinven Limited. Cinven is a private equity firm engaged in the provision of investment management and investment advisory services to a number of investment funds. The controlled companies in Cinven’s portfolio of investments are active in a variety of sectors including business services, consumer, financial services, healthcare, industrials and technology, media and telecommunications.

determination_table_content.details:
Alter Domus Nederland B.V. (Alter Domus) applied for a notification
waiver in respect of its (or an indirect, wholly owned subsidiary of
Alter Domus Global S.à r.l.) proposed acquisition of 100% of the
issued share capital in MSC Group Co Pty Ltd (MSC), as described in
the transaction documents provided as part of the application (the
Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

The acquirer, Alter Domus, is a global provider of fund
administration, private debt administration, and corporate services,
dedicated exclusively to the alternative investment industry, with
more than 6,500 staff across 39 offices worldwide. In Australia, Alter
Domus is focused on fund administration for wholesale fund
managers targeting wholesale investors in the alternative
investments space.
Alter Domus is indirectly controlled by the Eighth Cinven Fund which
is managed and controlled by Cinven Limited. Cinven is a private
equity firm engaged in the provision of investment management and
investment advisory services to a number of investment funds. The
controlled companies in Cinven’s portfolio of investments are active
in a variety of sectors including business services, consumer,
financial services, healthcare, industrials and technology, media and
telecommunications
The target, MSC Group, is an Australian-headquartered provider of
professional trustee, custody, financial intermediary and fund
administration services. Its core business is in the provision of
custody and trustee services, with ancillary service offerings
including fund administration.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver and had regard
to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers
that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening
of competition. In particular:
a. there is a small horizontal overlap between Alter Domus and
MSC in the supply of fund administration services in
Australia, and the increase in share of supply arising from
the Acquisition is expected to be small
b. there are alternative suppliers of fund administration
services in Australia
c. there is a low risk of foreclosure or other concerning vertical
or conglomerate effects.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
